comparator.name: Religious Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-taught full-time bachelor comprises 60 EC per year, including some English-taught courses. The adopted 2026–2027 programme regulation lists Arabic first among the permitted first-year subject packages; the dated guide specifies its four 6 EC language courses. This neutral illustration retains the common Religious Studies curriculum, 30 EC of open choice and an 18 EC thesis trajectory. It excludes the shortened programme and other first-year packages. The degree has no formal graduation tracks.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The verified route includes mythology, sacred images, popular culture and the cultural history of countercultures. The selected programme gives students successive methods to interpret religious narrative, ritual and material culture. Political rights, conflict and identity already contribute to the core. The political alternative moves into general institutions without sustained coursework on religion as a political institution. Philosophy and literature address spirituality and identity, but a separate curriculum in contemporary lived religion would require empirical study of religious communities and practices.

audience.programmeDescription: Students study religious diversity, traditions, texts and practices through historical, literary and social-scientific approaches. They examine contemporary religion and spirituality, Western esotericism and religion in Amsterdam. The reviewed pathway includes first-year Arabic.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination studies religious meaning through myth, art, objects and ritual. Amsterdam also teaches several religious traditions, Arabic, lived religion and specialist research in religious studies.
